newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Airports unaware of privatisation bid.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Airports unaware of privatisation bid.

text.p: Malaysia Airports Bhd's chairman said that he was not aware of a bid by Malaysian Helicopter Services Bhd to privatise the company, the Business Times reported on Friday.
"We are not aware of any of these (plans)," Basir Ismail, Malaysia Airports chairman, was quoted by the daily as saying.

The Asian Wall Street Journal reported on Aug. 29 that Malaysian Helicopter, which is controlled by Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) chairman Tajudin Ramli, had received government approval to bid for the company which manages Malaysia's airport facilities.

Malaysian Helicopter confirmed it is interested in buying the airport company. In a brief statement released late on Thursday to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, Malaysian Helicopter said it "has expressed interest" in the airport company under the country's privatisation programme.
State-owned Malaysia Airports manages 19 airports around the country and holds the rights to operate duty-free outlets at the airports.
